newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU opens in-depth probe of BT-MCI merger.
newsitem.headline: EU opens in-depth probe of BT-MCI merger.

text.p: The European Commission said Thursday it had opened an in-depth probe into the $20 billion merger between British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp.
The European Union's executive body said it needed more time to decide whether the deal would unfairly restrict competition for U.S.-European telecommunications traffic.
"The commission's enquiries suggest a certain number of areas in which further investigations are required," it said in a statement.

These included whether the merger would impair the competitive position of major rivals on the British-U.S. route, unfairly divert U.S.-European traffic through Britain or restrict the availability of trans-Atlantic cable capacity, it said.
"The impact of the merger on the teleconferencing market will also need to be carefully examined," the commission added.

The alliance between British Telecom and the No. 2 U.S. long distance company was submitted to the commission for clearance in December under EU merger rules banning creation or strengthening of dominant positions.

Thursday was the deadline for the Commission to decide whether to clear the deal after its preliminary inquiry or launch an in-depth probe if it was worried about the impact on fair competition in Europe.

The commission probe, which could last up to four months, seemed to pose little danger for the alliance itself, which still faces its main regulatory challenge on the other side of the Atlantic, industry sources and antitrust lawyers have said.
Telecommunications giant AT&T Corp. has demanded that the approval of the operation be made subject to competitive safeguards and commitments regarding fair pricing and equal access to phone lines.

The commission cleared a joint venture between British Telecom and MCI in 1994 under different EU competition rules that apply to alliances that are looser than mergers. That link-up, known as Concert, was created to provide enhanced telecommunications services to multinational companies.

The commission last year approved the Global One alliance formed by France Telecom, Deutsche Telekom and Sprint Corp., but only after receiving assurances from France and Germany that they would open the market for telecommunications network infrastructure to competition.

The commission last month said it was ready to clear the Uniworld telecommunications alliance between AT&T and the Unisource joint venture involving the Spanish, Dutch, Swedish and Swiss phone companies -- after winning market-opening pledges from Spain and Switzerland.
